item.title: China's Long March-12 rocket launches new internet satellite group
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
WENCHANG, Hainan, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- China launched a Long March-12 carrier rocket on Saturday from a commercial spacecraft launch site in the southern island province of Hainan, sending an internet satellite group into space.
The rocket lifted off at 3:27 a.m. (Beijing Time) and successfully placed the payload, the 27th group of low-orbit internet satellites, into the preset orbit.

item.title: China warns against trade protectionism under "overcapacity" pretext: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
BEIJING, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- China opposes trade protectionism under the pretext of so-called "overcapacity" and will respond as necessary if relevant economies adopt measures that harm Chinese interests, a spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce said on Friday.
The spokesperson made the remarks in response to a media question about an announcement by the Office of the United States Trade Representative on Wednesday that the United States had convened senior officials from 14 other economies to sign a joint ministerial statement on so-called "structural excess capacity and production."
China has repeatedly clarified its position on the so-called "overcapacity" matter on various occasions and released a dedicated position paper in July, the spokesperson said.
The country has consistently maintained that production capacity issues should be viewed in a comprehensive, objective and fair manner, rather than politicizing economic and trade matters out of concerns over one's own industrial competitiveness and market position, according to the spokesperson.
The spokesperson stressed that China opposes attempts by certain countries to pursue trade protectionism in the name of addressing so-called "overcapacity," warning that such practices would only disrupt the global economic and trade order, undermine the stability of global industrial and supply chains, and pose long-term risks to global economic growth.
If relevant economies use the issue as a pretext to take steps that harm China's interests, China will take necessary measures in response, the spokesperson added.
China remains committed to building a modern industrial system through openness and cooperation and supports the establishment of a fair and equitable international economic order, the spokesperson noted.
The spokesperson called on all parties to uphold multilateralism, promote mutually beneficial cooperation, respect the laws of the market economy, and jointly safeguard an open and inclusive framework for cooperation across global industrial and supply chains.

item.title: China, EU agree to keep bilateral trade ties stable, hold next meeting in March 2027
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
BEIJING, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- China and the European Union (EU) have agreed to maintain stable bilateral economic and trade ties and make them more balanced, while scheduling March 2027 for their next meeting under a trade and investment consultation mechanism, according to a joint statement released Friday.
Published by China's Ministry of Commerce, the statement said that Chinese Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao and European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maros Sefcovic jointly chaired the second meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism from Thursday to Friday in Beijing.
The two sides engaged in pragmatic and productive discussions and agreed on a list of outcomes, the ministry said. The list set out 16 specific points of consensus covering trade and investment balance, export controls, intellectual property rights and World Trade Organization (WTO) reform.
According to the ministry, the two sides agreed to continue exploring the possibility of reducing tariffs on certain goods within the framework of WTO rules.
China and the EU reached an understanding on trade in hybrid vehicles in a manner consistent with WTO rules. The two sides will also continue relevant procedures concerning companies' price undertakings and reviews in the EU's anti-subsidy case involving Chinese electric vehicles, the ministry said.
The two sides further agreed to hold a technical dialogue on the EU's Foreign Subsidies Regulation.
China expressed its willingness to continue facilitating the processing of export license applications for rare earths and permanent magnets destined for the EU through a "green channel" mechanism. The EU, together with its member states, will continue to facilitate the resolution of key licensing cases involving China in the dual-use sector, according to the ministry.
The two sides also agreed to explore investment cooperation to promote their respective economic development and discussed future-oriented cooperation.
As key trading partners, China and the EU reaffirmed their commitment to properly handling their differences within the framework of WTO rules, and to keeping bilateral economic and trade ties stable and making them more balanced, the ministry noted.
The two sides also agreed to hold the third meeting of the consultation mechanism in March next year and maintain close communication in the meantime, including through a ministerial video conference in January next year, the ministry said.
Both sides viewed the second meeting as a new starting point for deepening China-EU cooperation and tasked their working teams with advancing follow-up work, promoting the early implementation of the agreed outcomes, and preparing for the third meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, according to the ministry.

item.title: China issues guidelines on developing new quality productive forces
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
BEIJING, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- The Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council have issued a set of guidelines aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces to bolster high-quality development.
These guidelines outline 19 key measures in five areas, namely advancing scientific and technological innovation, deepening the integration of sci-tech and industrial innovation, innovating development approaches, promoting institutional and mechanism innovation, and improving mechanisms for talent development.
Noting that developing new quality productive forces is an intrinsic requirement and an important focus of promoting high-quality development, these guidelines stress the importance of innovation-driven development, reform and measures tailored to local conditions, and following the approach of "establishing the new before abolishing the old."
The guidelines call for pursuing high technology, high efficiency and high quality, properly handling the relationships between the government and the market, between the qualitative nature of productive forces and the forms they take in industry and business, between reform and development, and between self-reliance and opening up, while coordinating development and security.
"The new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation has opened up broad prospects for developing new quality productive forces. Seizing this historic opportunity requires moving faster to achieve greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology and raising innovation capacity across the board to maintain strategic initiative," said Wang Shengxiao, a researcher with the Party School of the Communist Party of China Central Committee.
The guidelines call for stronger original and transformative sci-tech innovation, with major sci-tech projects to focus on strategic, landmark and leading products, targeting the cutting-edge of global science and technology and serving major areas of economic development, major national needs, and people's health.
They stress the need for faster breakthroughs in key core technologies, including efforts to promote the high-quality development of key manufacturing industrial chains and implement industrial innovation projects in priority areas.
The guidelines emphasize coordinated efforts to strengthen national strategic sci-tech capabilities, giving full play to national laboratories in organizing major national sci-tech projects and building major innovation platforms. The guidelines also urge optimizing the roles and distribution of national sci-tech research institutions, high-level research universities and leading sci-tech enterprises.
The guidelines underline the principal role of enterprises in sci-tech innovation, encouraging technology-based small and medium-sized enterprises to increase research and development investment and supporting capable private enterprises in taking the lead in major national technological breakthrough tasks.
To speed up the transformation of sci-tech achievements into real productive forces, the guidelines call for leveraging the advantages of China's vast market to better connect technology with the market and advance the development of new quality productive forces on a larger scale.
The guidelines also urge upgrading traditional industries through the application of digital, intelligent and green technologies.
The country should seek to advance producer services toward greater specialization and the higher end of the value chain, while improving the quality, diversity and convenience of consumer services, according to the guidelines.
For emerging industries, the guidelines emphasize efforts to foster their growth and develop new pillar industries. The guidelines encourage greater cross-industry and cross-regional integration, measures to avoid "involution-style" competition, and support eastern regions to help central, western and northeastern regions develop emerging industries in line with local conditions.
The guidelines call for forward-looking planning for future industries and emphasize the need to make full use of existing fiscal policies to support their development and guide social capital to steadily increase investment.
The guidelines also urge promoting the deep integration of the digital economy and the real economy, optimizing the layout, construction and operation of national data infrastructure, advancing the digital transformation of the manufacturing sector, and building digital industrial clusters with international competitiveness.
The guidelines call for fully implementing the "AI Plus" initiative, using artificial intelligence (AI) to transform traditional industries, accelerating innovation in AI and other digital and intelligent technologies, and promoting the widespread application of AI across industries.
Efforts are also needed to establish systems for technology monitoring, early risk warning and emergency response to ensure that AI is safe, reliable and controllable, the guidelines note.
These guidelines further propose building a green, low-carbon and circular economic system by strengthening green manufacturing, developing green services, expanding the green energy industry, and driving the supply of green products via green consumption.
Efforts should be made to optimize the policy toolbox for green development and implement fiscal, financial, investment, pricing, technological and environmental policies that promote green and low-carbon development, according to the guidelines.
The country will actively advance the energy revolution and accelerate the green transition of energy use in production and daily life across society, the guidelines add.
The guidelines call for deepening reform to promote close integration of science and technology with the economy, saying that efforts should be made to build an open, shared and secure nationally integrated data market.
The guidelines also stress the need to improve the market regulation system and increase the supply of innovative financial products.
The guidelines pledge to allocate advanced production factors globally by expanding high-standard opening up and actively building a global innovation cooperation network, and encouraging foreign venture capital institutions, international standards organizations and others to develop in China.
The guidelines urge cultivating talent urgently needed for the development of new quality productive forces, adding that policies on the use and flow of talent should be improved.
"New quality productive forces are primarily driven by transformational technological breakthroughs, which bring profound changes to how innovation is organized, industries evolve and resources are allocated," said Liu Zhenzhong, a researcher at the Institute of Industrial and Technological Economics of the National Development and Reform Commission. "These changes require deeper reforms to reshape institutional frameworks and remove obstacles to development."
The outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) identifies the development of new quality productive forces as a key strategic task and sets out 28 major projects related to this goal, accounting for 25.7 percent of the 109 major projects outlined in the plan.
The projects focus on four priorities: strengthening industrial capabilities and competitiveness, fostering emerging industries, pursuing breakthroughs in cutting-edge technologies, and enhancing innovation capabilities.
At an international seminar held in Beijing in September, Chinese experts said China's development of new quality productive forces could provide fresh momentum for global economic growth and create new opportunities for countries at different stages of modernization. Abdulrahman Bello Dambazau, Nigeria's ambassador to China, noted that the emphasis on talent development, scientific research and industrial upgrading could offer useful reference for developing countries.
China's development of high-tech, green and intelligent industries is also creating more opportunities for cross-border investment and industrial cooperation. At the China International Fair for Investment and Trade in September, representatives from European countries explored cooperation with China in areas such as clean energy, AI, smart manufacturing, biomedicine and the digital economy.

item.title: China records 826 mln domestic tourist trips during 2026 National Day holiday amid diverse offerings
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Tourists view a giant floral basket installation at Tian'anmen Square in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 1, 2026. China recorded 826 million domestic tourist trips during the seven-day National Day holiday, with tourism spending totaling 738.38 billion yuan (about 109.67 billion U.S. dollars), the Ministry of Culture and Tourism said Friday. On a daily average basis, the number of domestic trips rose 6.3 percent from the eight-day National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival holiday in 2025, while tourism spending increased 4.3 percent, according to the ministry. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong)
BEIJING, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- China saw 826 million domestic tourist trips during the recent seven-day National Day holiday, with tourism spending totaling 738.38 billion yuan (about 109.67 billion U.S. dollars), the Ministry of Culture and Tourism said on Friday.
The holiday witnessed a vibrant cultural scene, with 180 large-scale performances held nationwide, including 125 concerts and 55 music festivals.
Beyond cultural performances, the integration of tourism with culture, commerce and sports continued to deepen. Mass-participation sports events and digital innovations offered visitors new experiences and helped drive tourism-related consumption.
Meanwhile, around 40 percent of tourists visited revolutionary sites or took part in activities such as flag-raising ceremonies and patriotic performances.
This trend takes on added significance this year, which marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March (1934-1936). The arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution.
Dai Bin, president of the China Tourism Academy, said the flow of visitors to revolutionary landmarks reflects people's emotional identification with revolutionary traditions.
When they travel, they don't just want to see history. They also want to draw deeper inspiration from the revolutionary legacy for their lives today, Dai noted.
Measures to boost tourism consumption have also helped expand holiday options for visitors and enhance their travel experiences.
Under a nationwide cultural and tourism consumption campaign running from late September through October, local authorities have organized a variety of activities and distributed more than 310 million yuan in consumption subsidies.
Tourists in traditional costumes take selfies at the Hetou Old Street scenic area in Fengnan District of Tangshan City, north China's Hebei Province, Oct. 1, 2026.
On a daily average basis, the number of domestic trips rose 6.3 percent from the eight-day National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival holiday in 2025, while tourism spending increased 4.3 percent, according to the ministry. (Xinhua/Mu Yu)
Tourists visit the Handan Museum in Handan, north China's Hebei Province, Oct. 2, 2026.
On a daily average basis, the number of domestic trips rose 6.3 percent from the eight-day National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival holiday in 2025, while tourism spending increased 4.3 percent, according to the ministry. (Photo by Hao Qunying/Xinhua)

item.title: Where the Long March began, China's new journey unfolds
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
An aerial drone photo taken on Aug. 18, 2026 shows a view of Yudu County, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Xinhua/Zhou Mi)
NANCHANG, Oct. 8 (Xinhua) -- The former ferry crossing is about half an hour's walk from the home of Sun Guanfa, 77, in Yudu, a hilly county in east China's Jiangxi Province.
For his father, the journey from this riverbank more than nine decades ago was part of an epic.
In October 1934, some 86,000 soldiers of the Red Army crossed the Yudu River to embark on what later came to be known as the Long March.
In a country beset by foreign invasion, social turmoil and destitution, the fledgling Red Army, led by the Communist Party of China (CPC), was fighting for national independence and the liberation of the Chinese people. But at the time, it was encircled by the overwhelming and much better-armed Kuomintang forces.
What followed was an epic military maneuver: from Yudu, Red Army troops trekked roughly 12,500 kilometers across China, crossing snow-covered mountains and treacherous marshlands, all the while battling enemy forces. They eventually reached the country's northwest, where, in 1936, they were joined by several other Red Army branches, marking the victorious conclusion of the Long March.
This military maneuver preserved the Red Army. It also gave the CPC a new foothold in northwest China, from which it built up its strength, fought back against invading Japanese troops and eventually toppled the corrupt Kuomintang regime, leading to the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949.
In Yudu, the Long March is not simply a chapter in a history book. It is a family story.
More than 17,000 residents joined the departing army. Only 277 were recorded as eventually returning home, said Zhong Min, a guide at a museum built beside the river to commemorate the departure.
Her voice still catches when she says that number.
Her maternal great-grandfather died fighting the encirclement campaigns. Her husband's grandfather marched away with the troops and was never heard from again. Sun's father fell in a battle that saw the forces of the Red Army reduced to just over 30,000.
"We are not telling other people's stories," Zhong said. "We are telling our own families'."
Here, the Long March is measured not only in kilometers and battles, but in the people who left home knowing they might never return.
For Sun, the legacy of that generation is deeply personal. Under a local tradition, Sun was adopted as the son of the soldier who left the riverbank and never returned, so that the soldier's family line could continue.
"People of my father's generation were willing to give their lives so ordinary people could be liberated," Sun said.
On the same riverbank in 2019, Chinese President Xi Jinping spoke of what had enabled the Party and the Red Army to come back from the brink of destruction time and again: firm ideals and convictions, and strong willpower.
"We must not forget our Party's original aspiration and founding mission," said Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission. The Party's long-stated mission, dating to its founding in 1921, is to seek happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation.
During the visit, Xi placed a flower basket at a monument commemorating the Red Army's departure and bowed in tribute. He then walked behind the monument to a railing overlooking the river and stood there for a long while.
The river remains. For Xi, it was also a place from which to look ahead to China's future.
"We came to this place to revisit what it was like when the Red Army set out," he told local people gathered nearby. "Today we are on a new journey -- to build a modern socialist country. We must carry on the work of those who came before us, gear up anew, and set out once more."
That new journey was unfolding against a vastly changed backdrop. When Xi visited Yudu, the nationwide campaign he had launched to combat poverty was entering its final stage.
It would culminate in the elimination of absolute poverty in a nation of 1.4 billion. Nearly 100 million rural residents were lifted out of poverty under Xi's "targeted poverty alleviation" campaign, which mobilized the entire Party and the nation.
Xi announced the victory, as a key part of building a moderately prosperous society in all respects, in 2021 when the CPC marked its centenary.
A drone photo taken on Oct. 2, 2026 shows tourists at a memorial hall marking the departure of the Long March by the Central Red Army in Yudu County, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Photo by Zeng Xiaomao/Xinhua)
During his 2019 visit, Xi saw for himself whether the former revolutionary base areas were on track to meet their poverty-reduction targets.
At Sun's home, he walked through the main hall to the backyard and checked the kitchen and the bedrooms. There was rice and cooking oil in the kitchen, and the bathroom was clean.
Xi asked about the family's income and how Sun's son and daughter-in-law made a living, where their children went to school, and what the school meals were like.
"By the time they grow up, we will have achieved the rejuvenation of our nation," Xi said, pointing to Sun's two grandchildren.
China aims to basically realize socialist modernization by 2035 and build a great modern socialist country in all respects by the middle of this century, according to the vision set by the Party.
Earlier, at the museum where Zhong served as a guide, Xi had stopped before a map of China made from straw sandals.
The display recalled how local people worked through the night to make straw sandals for the soldiers, many of whom fought barefoot. They also dismantled doors, bed boards, roof beams and even timber intended for coffins to build pontoon bridges, helping the soldiers cross the Yudu River.
"The country has developed and people's lives have improved, but we must remember where it all came from," Xi said. "We must not forget our revolutionary forefathers and those who died for the revolution, or the people of the old revolutionary base areas."
Nowadays, golden waves of selenium-rich rice ripple around the 700-year-old village, and rows of modern vegetable greenhouses stand nearby. In the residential area, white-walled houses with gray-tiled roofs sit amid trees, while pavilions nestle between them.
"Now we have wages from working, rent from our guesthouses and dividends from our shares," Sun said. "Our annual income has tripled to more than 200,000 yuan (around 29,000 U.S. dollars)."
This file photo taken on Oct. 21, 2020 shows Sun Guanfa (L) introducing local agricultural products to tourists in Tantou Village, Yudu County, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Xinhua/Wan Xiang)
The transformation extends well beyond Yudu.
Much of southern Jiangxi, once cut off from the outside world by rugged mountains, is far more connected. High-speed rail links it with the city of Shenzhen, the country's economic powerhouse close to Hong Kong. Expressways also reach every county, and paved roads now extend into villages.
For local business owners, it no longer means spending two days and two nights on the road to source a critical part. Now they can hop on a high-speed train, pick up what they need in the morning and return that afternoon, drastically speeding up the development of a prototype.
The change is not only about getting around. Industries such as non-ferrous metals and advanced materials, electronics and information technology, and textiles and apparel have taken root here. For ordinary people, the changes are closer to home. Housing has improved, drinking water is safer, and schools and medical care are more accessible.
More people can now earn a living without leaving their hometowns. In March, the Hong Kong Polytechnic University launched a facility dedicated to research into smart wearables and smart clothing in Xingguo, a county next to Yudu.
This summer, Yudu welcomed students from more than 170 universities across China who came to retrace the Long March at the places where it began. Many realized that the Red Army soldiers who set out were their age.
"Standing where those young soldiers began their journey gave me a deeper understanding of what they accomplished," said Liu Fanshuo, an undergraduate studying automation.
Today, five modern bridges span the Yudu River near the crossings where local people once built pontoon bridges to help the Red Army cross.
On the banks, Sun pours hot tea for tourists whose lives might have been very different had those soldiers never crossed.

item.title: Another Nanjing Massacre survivor dies, only 20 remain
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Another survivor of the Nanjing Massacre died on Wednesday, reducing the number of registered living survivors to 20, the Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders said.
Massacre survivor Guo Xiulan died at the age of 94, according to the memorial hall in Nanjing, the capital of east China's Jiangsu Province.
Guo was born in 1932. According to survivor recollections documented by the museum, when the Nanjing Massacre took place after Japanese troops captured Nanjing on December 13, 1937, Guo's parents took their three children to hide in an underground shelter along with neighbors.
"Japanese soldiers stood at the opening and strafed it with machine guns. My parents and my youngest sister perished. Only my second sister and I survived," Guo was recorded as saying.
The Nanjing Massacre unfolded over six weeks. Japanese soldiers killed approximately 300,000 Chinese civilians and unarmed soldiers in one of the most barbaric atrocities of World War II.
Over the years, the number of survivors able to share firsthand accounts of the massacre has continued to decline.
In 2014, China's top legislature designated December 13 as the national memorial day for the victims of the Nanjing Massacre. The Chinese government has also preserved survivors' testimonies through written records and video recordings.
Documents related to the massacre were inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register in 2015. To date, only 20 living survivors of the Nanjing Massacre remain on the registry maintained by the Nanjing Association for Assistance to Victims of Japanese Aggression and Inheritance of Nanjing Massacre Historical Memory.

item.title: Immersive experiences fuel inbound tourism boom over China's National Day holiday
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Foreign tourists at the Palace Museum in Beijing, China, October 6, 2026. /VCG
China's inbound tourism market is seeing robust growth during the 2026 National Day holiday.
China's border crossings are expected to handle an average of about 2.15 million passenger trips per day during the holiday, according to the National Immigration Administration.
Data from Chinese online travel agency Trip.com showed that inbound tourist trips during the combine holiday posted double digit year-on-year growth for the first time.
New trends are emerging in China's inbound tourism market, as overseas visitors move beyond traditional sightseeing, and increasingly immerse themselves in local life, culture and experiences.
Orders for one-day inbound tours surged more than fourfold year on year, while scenic spot ticket bookings jumped over 220%. Cultural attractions accounted for around 43% of inbound scenic spot bookings during the combined holiday, up from about 32% in 2024.
Russian tourist learned black tea brewing in Huzhou, Zhejiang Province, China, June 5, 2026. /VCG
Traditional Chinese style photo shoots have also become a new source of tourism spending among foreign visitors. At Shanghai's Yu Garden, a popular destination for foreign tourists, they are dressing in traditional Chinese hanfu and taking ancient style photos against a backdrop of upturned eaves and traditional pavilions, embracing a new way to experience Eastern aesthetics.
Cultural performances are also offering foreign visitors new ways to experience and understand China. In Zhangjiajie, central China's Hunan Province, shows such as "Charming Xiangxi" blend intangible cultural heritage with real mountain and water scenery, modern lighting and multilingual subtitles. By the end of September, the "Charming Xiangxi" theater had welcomed more than 140,000 overseas visitors this year.
The "Charming Xiangxi" performance in Zhangjiajie, Hunan Province, China, October 4, 2026. /VCG
In Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, the Huaqiangbei electronics market has emerged as a popular tech shopping destination for overseas visitors, who are captivated by AI translation glasses, smartwatches, humanoid robots, portable AI speakers and panoramic cameras.
The surge in inbound tourism was fueled by China's expanding visa-free policies.
During this year's Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, from September 25 to 27, foreign nationals made 728,000 border crossings, up 37.7% year on year. Among inbound foreign visitors, a total of 247,000 entered under visa-free policies, an increase of 32.7% from a year earlier, data from the National Immigration Administration showed.
Foreign tourists arrive at Shanghai Pudong International Airport in Shanghai, China, September 30, 2026. /VCG
The growth in inbound travel is driven by the ongoing innovation in China's tourism offerings, experiences and consumption scenarios, giving international visitors more opportunities to engage with local culture and everyday life, said Li Xinjian, executive dean of the Capital Culture and Tourism Development Research Institute at Beijing International Studies University.
Li added that China is increasingly becoming a destination where travelers can not only see the sights, but also immerse themselves in the experience.

item.title: Flag-raising ceremony held at Tian'anmen Square to celebrate 77th founding anniversary of PRC
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
A flag-raising ceremony to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China (PRC) was held at Tian'anmen Square in Beijing on Thursday.
The Guard of Honor of the Chinese People's Liberation Army escorted the national flag to the square, while the military band played the national anthem.
Many people from across China gathered at the square to watch the ceremony.

item.title: Activities held across China to celebrate National Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Cities across China are decorating landmark sites with national flags and floral displays as National Day arrives, and people hold various activities to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.
